title: go-sdk: streaming decoding DSL with typed structs and retry composables
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: our existing Go SDK provides low-level streaming primitives but lacks a concise, typed developer UX for decoding structured outputs from streaming LLM responses and composing retry/backpressure behavior. Engineers repeatedly hand-roll ad-hoc decoders that either rebuffer the whole stream or incorrectly handle partial JSON tokens, leading to bugs and GC pressure.

Goal: deliver a small, well-tested streaming decoding DSL and set of generic helpers that let callers declare typed structs (e.g., ResponseEnvelope[T]) and decode tokens incrementally with first-class support for: (1) partial JSON frames, (2) chunk-level idempotent retry, (3) backpressure-aware reading, and (4) ergonomic examples and migration guidance. The work should be API-stable and opt-in behind a minor SDK version (go-sdk-2.4).
background: Context from audits and customer issues: several customers reported subtle deserialization errors when using streaming structured output for function-calls and tool responses. We also observed elevated GC and allocation overhead on high-throughput chat workloads when streaming responses were fully buffered for decode. Prior tickets (ENG-41234, ENG-27143) introduced typed response mappers but didn't solve chunked/partial streaming semantics or provide composable retry middleware. This ticket consolidates a robust approach designed for production workloads.
acceptance_criteria: A generics-based Decode[T] API that accepts an io.Reader (stream) and returns a channel or iterator of typed events without buffering the full response
StreamDecoder supports incremental JSON token stitching and recovers cleanly from mid-chunk boundaries across network frames
A RetryPolicyStack composable that can: retry idempotent requests at request-level; optionally replay last N decoded tokens on retry for resumable outputs; and integrates with HTTP 429/5xx semantics
Backpressure-aware StreamReader that exposes a controllable internal buffer and exposes metrics (bytes_in_buffer, average_lag_ms) compatible with Console telemetry
Comprehensive unit tests and integration tests (mock server + live benchmark) covering token-splitting, partial JSON, retry replay, and error cases
Migration guide + two short examples: (a) typed chat messages streaming into ResponseEnvelope[Message], (b) function-call structured outputs decoding to ToolResult structs
Benchmarks showing no >15% regression in median end-to-end latency over current master for typical chat workloads; memory allocations improved for long-response streaming cases
API documented in SDK README and small snippet added to quickstart examples repo
implementation_notes: Introduce package redwood/streamutil with: StreamDecoder[T], DecodeStream[T], and UnmarshalPartial[T] helpers using Go generics
StreamDecoder core design: internal byte buffer; token boundary scanner that uses encoding/json.Decoder.Token when possible and a lightweight tail-buffer to merge cross-frame tokens
Provide two reading modes: 'push' (channel of T) and 'pull' (Iterator.Next() T, error) for different ergonomics

RetryPolicyStack: middleware chain for Request -> ResponseStream. Implement IdempotentRetry (request-level), ChunkResume (replay last k tokens on retry), and BackoffStrategy with jitter. Allow policies to be composed by callers
Backpressure: StreamReader exposes a MaxBufferedBytes config and blocks the underlying network reader when buffer > MaxBufferedBytes. Expose context cancellation for abrupt shutdowns
APIs must be Go 1.20+ compatible. Avoid using runtime/trace-heavy allocations. Keep reflect usage minimal; rely on generics where possible
Expose internal metrics via the SDK metrics interface: stream.buffered_bytes, stream.retry_count, stream.decode_errors, stream.avg_token_latency
Add migration helpers: FromLegacyStream(reader io.Reader) -> StreamDecoder[legacyType] with compatibility layer for current decode helpers
Examples: two example programs in examples/streaming/ typed_chat_stream.go and function_tool_stream.go demonstrating cancellation, retry hooks, and console metric tagging
Documentation: README section 'Streaming structured output (Go)' with small code snippets and pitfalls when using partial JSON and retries
test_plan: Unit tests: coverage for token-splitting, incomplete Unicode sequences, and malformed chunk boundaries
Integration tests: mock HTTP server that emits frames with artificial splits and delay; test chunk-resume semantics and replay correctness
Fuzz test: feed random chunk boundaries with valid JSON payloads to ensure decoder never panics and returns deterministic errors
Benchmarks: run existing chat workload benchmark harness (100 concurrent streams) and measure median latency and allocations; target <=15% regressions
Canary rollout: publish go-sdk-2.4-beta tag and run internal services (growth sandbox) with feature flag for 2 days before full rollout
Run static analysis (go vet, staticcheck) and add lint rules for any new exported API
risks: Compatibility risk: changing stream decode semantics may break callers that assume whole-message buffering. Mitigation: opt-in API and migration helper functions
Performance regressions under GC pressure if buffer strategy is naive. Mitigation: tune MaxBufferedBytes default and benchmark with representative payloads

Complexity: Retry/replay semantics for non-idempotent side-effects are tricky. Mitigation: clearly document that ChunkResume only applies to idempotent or replay-safe protocols and provide hooks to mark events as non-replayable
Edge cases: partial UTF-8 sequences across chunk boundaries might be expensive to repair. Mitigation: use minimal reassembly buffer and inline checks; add unit tests
Security: ensure telemetry doesn't leak user content. Mitigation: sanitize any telemetry fields and keep example payloads synthetic
